@@ -216,6 +216,48 @@ configuration in :setting:`DATABASES`::
 
 .. _isolation level: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html
 
+Role setting
+------------
+The PostgreSQL permission model consists of roles, which can represent
+users or groups. Each database object (table, sequence, view, etc...)
+is assigned an owning role and that owner is the only role that can
+modify or drop those objects. If the Django application is running using
+temporary credentials from an external credential management system then
+that temporary role will not match the owning role for the database
+objects and migrations or other structural mutations to the database
+objects will fail with permission errors.
+
+To solve this, create a role that acts as a group within the database
+that can own those objects then create your individual user roles as
+members of that owning role.::
+
+  CREATE ROLE my_application_role;
+  CREATE ROLE temporary_user_role IN ROLE my_application_role;
+
+Setting the ``assume_role`` option in the :setting:`OPTIONS` of your
+database configuration in :setting:`DATABASES`. This will cause Django
+to issue a ``SET ROLE`` statement during connection creation which will
+cause the logged-in user to assume the group role which has owner access
+to those database objects.
+
+.. code-block:: python
+    :caption: ``settings.py``
+
+    DATABASES = {
+        'default': {
+            'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.postgresql',
+            'OPTIONS': {
+                'assume_role': 'my_application_role',
+            },
+        }
+    }
+
+.. note::
+
+   If the database was created before the introduction of a grouping role then
+   object ownership may be inconsistent which will result in permission errors
+   until the ownership of each object is updated.

body:
Ah yeah, it looks like this is documented behavior of [SET](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/8.4/sql-set.html)

> If SET (or equivalently SET SESSION) is issued within a transaction that is later aborted, the effects of the SET command disappear when the transaction is rolled back. Once the surrounding transaction is committed, the effects will persist until the end of the session, unless overridden by another SET.

Fixed.
